subject: Maths
title: Year 9 Maths Exam 5
intro: Answer every question. You may use a calculator, but show your working in the working box so you can get method marks.

questions.q: Which value of x is not a solution of 4x − 3 ≥ 9?
questions.ms: Answer: C: 2.9 (the solution is x ≥ 3). B1.

questions.q: Which is x2 − 9x + 20 factorised?
questions.ms: Answer: A: (x − 4)(x − 5). B1.

questions.q: Which equation has solutions x = 3 and x = −2?
questions.ms: Answer: B: x² − x − 6 = 0. B1.

questions.q: List all the integers that satisfy −7 ≤ 3x − 1 < 8
questions.hint: Type the values from smallest to largest, separated by commas, like -2,0,3
questions.ms: Answer: −2, −1, 0, 1, 2. M1 for −2 ≤ x < 3. A1 for −2, −1, 0, 1, 2 only (−2 included, 3 not).

questions.q:
Cinema tickets cost AED 45 for an adult and AED 30 for a child. A group of 2 adults and c children spends less than AED 300.
Write an inequality in c.
questions.hint: Type it like x>4 or -2<x<=3 (use <= for ≤ and >= for ≥)

questions.q: Work out the greatest number of children in the group. (children)
questions.ms: Answer: 6. M1 for 30c < 210 or c < 7. A1 for 6 (7 is not allowed because the inequality is strict).

questions.q:
A triangle has sides x cm, (x + 4) cm and (2x − 1) cm.
Its perimeter is more than 31 cm but no more than 43 cm.
Find all the possible integer values of x.
questions.hint: Type the values from smallest to largest, separated by commas, like -2,0,3
questions.ms: Answer: 8, 9, 10. M1 for perimeter 4x + 3. M1 for 31 < 4x + 3 ≤ 43 or 7 < x ≤ 10. A1 for 8, 9, 10.

questions.q: Expand and simplify (2x − 1)(x + 3)(x − 2)
questions.ms: Answer: 2x³ + x² − 13x + 6. M1 for one pair expanded correctly, e.g. 2x² + 5x − 3. M1 for multiplying by the third bracket with at most one error. A1 for 2x³ + x² − 13x + 6.

questions.q: Factorise fully 12x2 − 27
Factorise 4x2 + 4x − 15
questions.ms: Answer: (2x − 3)(2x + 5). M1 for brackets giving two of the three terms, or splitting 4x into 10x − 6x. A1 for (2x − 3)(2x + 5).

questions.q: Solve 3x2 − 14x + 8 = 0 by factorising.
questions.hint: Type both answers separated by a comma, like 1/2,-3
questions.ms: Answer: (3x − 2)(x − 4) = 0, so x = 2/3 or x = 4. M1 for (3x ± 2)(x ± 4). A1 for (3x − 2)(x − 4). A1 for x = 2/3 and x = 4.

questions.q: Solve (x + 2)2 = 5(x + 2). Give all the solutions.
questions.hint: Type both answers separated by a comma, like 3,-2
questions.ms: Answer: x = −2 or x = 3. M1 for (x + 2)(x + 2 − 5) = 0 or x² − x − 6 = 0. A1 for x = 3. A1 for x = −2 as well (dividing by x + 2 loses it).

questions.q: Solve 2x2 − 5x − 4 = 0. Give your answers to 2 decimal places.
questions.hint: Type both answers separated by a comma, like 3,-2
questions.ms: Answer: x = 3.14 or x = −0.64. M1 for correct substitution: (5 ± √(25 + 32)) / 4. M1 for √57 or 7.549… A1 for 3.14 and −0.64.

questions.q:
A firework is launched from the ground. Its height, h metres, after t seconds is h = 35t − 5t2.
How many seconds after launch does it land? (seconds)
questions.ms: Answer: 7 seconds. M1 for 5t(7 − t) = 0. A1 for 7.

questions.q: Find the maximum height of the firework. (m)
questions.ms: Answer: 61.25 m (at t = 3.5). M1 for t = 3.5. A1 for 61.25.

questions.q: For how many seconds is the firework at least 50 m above the ground? (seconds)
questions.ms: Answer: 3 seconds (from t = 2 to t = 5). M1 for 35t − 5t² = 50. M1 for t² − 7t + 10 = 0. A1 for t = 2 and t = 5. A1 for 3 seconds.

questions.q:
A quadratic curve crosses the x-axis at x = −3 and x = 7.
Write down the x-coordinate of its turning point.
questions.ms: Answer: x = 2. B1 for 2 (midway: (−3 + 7) ÷ 2).

questions.q: The curve is y = (x + 3)(x − 7). Find the y-coordinate of the turning point.
questions.ms: Answer: y = −25, so the turning point is (2, −25). M1 for (2 + 3)(2 − 7). A1 for −25.

questions.q:
A rectangular garden is (2x + 1) m long and (x + 3) m wide. Its area is 63 m2.
Show that 2x2 + 7x − 60 = 0
questions.ms: Answer: (2x + 1)(x + 3) = 2x² + 7x + 3 = 63, so 2x² + 7x − 60 = 0. M1 for (2x + 1)(x + 3) = 63. A1 for 2x² + 7x + 3 = 63 then rearranged.

questions.q: Find the perimeter of the garden. (m)
questions.ms: Answer: 32 m (x = 4, so 9 m by 7 m). M1 for solving (formula or (x − 4)(2x + 15) = 0). A1 for x = 4 (reject −7.5). M1 for sides 9 and 7. A1 for 32 m.

questions.q: Solve x2 + 2x − 15 ≥ 0
questions.hint: Type it like x<-1 or x>4 (use <= for ≤ and >= for ≥)
questions.ms: Answer: x ≤ −5 or x ≥ 3. M1 for (x + 5)(x − 3). M1 for critical values −5 and 3. A1 for x ≤ −5 or x ≥ 3.

questions.q: Prove that (n + 5)2 − (n + 1)2 is a multiple of 8 for every integer n.
questions.ms: Answer: n² + 10n + 25 − (n² + 2n + 1) = 8n + 24 = 8(n + 3). M1 for expanding both brackets. A1 for 8n + 24. A1 for 8(n + 3) with a conclusion.

questions.q: Prove that the product of two consecutive even numbers is always a multiple of 8.
questions.ms: Answer: 2n(2n + 2) = 4n(n + 1). One of n and n + 1 is even, so n(n + 1) = 2k and the product is 8k.. B1 for 2n and 2n + 2. M1 for 4n² + 4n or 4n(n + 1). M1 for explaining n(n + 1) is even. A1 for a complete conclusion (8 × something).
